method_card.title: Electrical Power and Energy Bills
steps: Pick the equation: P = VI (voltage and current), P = I²R (current and resistance), or E = QV (charge and voltage).
For bills, convert power to kilowatts (÷1,000) and time to hours first.
Energy (kWh) = power (kW) × time (h). Cost = energy × price per kWh.
State the answer with its unit: W, J, kWh, p or £.
method_card.content:
Two families of question live here: electrical power and energy bills.

Power: use P = VI when you know voltage and current, P = I²R when you know current and resistance, and E = QV for the energy a charge carries. Square the current before multiplying in P = I²R.

Bills: unit slips cost the most marks. Put power in kilowatts and time in hours, then energy (kWh) = power × time and cost = energy × price per kWh. There are 1,000 W in a kilowatt and 100 pence in a pound.

exam_context.frequency: High: power and energy cost calculations appear frequently

bronze.display: A toaster draws a current of 4 A from a 230 V supply. Calculate its power in watts.
bronze.hint: Multiply the voltage by the current.

misconceptions.message: Multiply, do not divide: P = V × I = 230 × 4 = 920 W.

guided_steps.say: Power from voltage and current: P = V × I. Volts and amps are already the base units, so nothing to convert.

guided_steps.hint: Two hundred and thirty times four.

guided_steps.pre: State it with the unit by checking: 920 ÷ 4 =
guided_steps.hint: Divide the power by the current; it should return the voltage.
guided_steps.done: 230 V comes back, so P = 920 W.

bronze.display: A 2 kW kettle is used for 0.5 hours. How many kWh does it use?
bronze.hint: Multiply the power in kW by the time in hours.

misconceptions.message: Energy is power times time: E = 2 × 0.5 = 1 kWh, not power divided by time.

guided_steps.say: Energy in kilowatt-hours = power (kW) × time (hours). Power is 2 kW and time 0.5 h, both already in the right units.

guided_steps.hint: Should return the power in kW.
guided_steps.done: 2 kW comes back, so E = 1 kWh.

bronze.display: A device uses 5 kWh and electricity costs 30p per kWh. Calculate the cost in pence.
bronze.hint: Multiply the number of units by the price of one unit.

misconceptions.message: Cost = energy × price = 5 × 30 = 150p. Do not divide.

guided_steps.say: Cost = energy (kWh) × price per kWh. The energy is 5 kWh and each kWh costs 30p.

guided_steps.hint: A hundred pence in a pound.

bronze.display: A resistor has resistance 20 Ω and carries a current of 2 A. Calculate the power dissipated.
bronze.hint: Square the current, then multiply by the resistance.

misconceptions.message: Square the current first: P = I²R = 2² × 20 = 4 × 20 = 80 W. Using 2 × 20 = 40 forgets the square.

guided_steps.say: For a resistor, P = I²R. Square the current before you multiply.

guided_steps.hint: Should give the squared current back.
guided_steps.done: 4 is 2², so I = 2 A. P = 80 W.

bronze.display: A charge of 200 C flows through a 6 V lamp. Calculate the energy transferred.
bronze.hint: Multiply the charge by the voltage.

misconceptions.message: Multiply the charge by the voltage: E = Q × V = 200 × 6 = 1,200 J. The charge alone is not the energy.

guided_steps.say: Energy carried by a charge: E = Q × V. Q is 200 C and V is 6 V.

bronze.equation_hint: Divide by 1,000 to convert W to kW
bronze.hint: There are 1,000 watts in a kilowatt.

misconceptions.message: To convert watts to kilowatts, divide by 1,000: 3,000 ÷ 1,000 = 3 kW. Multiplying gives 3,000,000, far too large.

guided_steps.say: To change watts to kilowatts, divide by 1,000. There are 1,000 watts in a kilowatt.

silver.display: A 1.5 kW hair dryer is used for 20 minutes each day for 30 days. How many kWh does it use in total?
silver.equation_hint: Convert minutes to hours first, then E = P × t
silver.hint: Find the total time in hours, then multiply by the power.

misconceptions.message: Convert to hours: 20 minutes a day for 30 days is 600 minutes, which is 10 hours. E = 1.5 × 10 = 15 kWh.
Use all 30 days, not one. The total time is 10 hours, so E = 1.5 × 10 = 15 kWh.

guided_steps.say: First get the total time in hours. The dryer runs 20 minutes a day for 30 days.

guided_steps.hint: Should return the power in kW.

silver.display: Electricity costs 28p per kWh. If the hair dryer above uses 15 kWh, calculate the cost in pounds.
silver.equation_hint: Cost (p) = energy × price. Then divide by 100 for £.
silver.hint: Work out the cost in pence, then divide by 100.

misconceptions.message: That is the cost in pence. Divide by 100 for pounds: 420 ÷ 100 = £4.20.

guided_steps.say: Cost = energy × price gives pence; divide by 100 for pounds. The dryer used 15 kWh at 28p each.

guided_steps.hint: A hundred pence in a pound.

silver.display: A resistor has resistance 50 Ω and carries 0.6 A. Calculate the power dissipated in watts.
silver.hint: Square the current first, even though it is a decimal.

misconceptions.message: Square the current: 0.6² = 0.36, then × 50 = 18 W. Using 0.6 × 50 = 30 forgets the square.

guided_steps.say: For a resistor, P = I²R. Square the current first, even when it is a decimal.

guided_steps.hint: Should give the squared current back.

silver.display: A 3 kW oven is used for 2.5 hours. Electricity costs 32p per kWh. Calculate the cost in pence.
silver.equation_hint: E = P × t, then cost = E × price
silver.hint: Find the energy in kWh first, then multiply by the price.

misconceptions.message: That is the energy in kWh. Multiply by the price to get the cost: 7.5 × 32 = 240p.

guided_steps.say: Two steps: energy first, then cost. Power 3 kW and time 2.5 h are already in the right units.

guided_steps.hint: Three times two and a half.
A hundred pence in a pound.

gold.display: A step-up transformer increases voltage from 25,000 V to 400,000 V. The primary current is 800 A. Calculate the secondary current in amperes.
gold.hint: Use Vp × Ip = Vs × Is and rearrange for the secondary current.

misconceptions.message: Vp × Ip = Vs × Is, so Is = (Vp × Ip) ÷ Vs = (25,000 × 800) ÷ 400,000 = 50 A. Dividing by the wrong voltage gives 12,800 A.

guided_steps.say: A transformer conserves power: Vp × Ip = Vs × Is. Rearrange for the secondary current: Is = (Vp × Ip) ÷ Vs. Check whether your board gives you this equation.

guided_steps.done: 20,000,000 W in and out, so Is = 50 A.

gold.display: A 900 W microwave is used for 8 minutes every day for 30 days. Electricity costs 30p per kWh. Calculate the total cost in pence.
gold.hint: Convert power to kW and total time to hours, then find the energy and cost.

misconceptions.message: Convert 900 W to 0.9 kW first. Skipping that gives 108,000, a thousand times too big.

guided_steps.say: Three moves: convert the power to kilowatts, get the total time in hours, then energy and cost.

gold.display: A cable with resistance 2 Ω carries a current of 100 A. Calculate the power wasted as heat in watts.
gold.hint: Square the current, then multiply by the resistance.

misconceptions.message: Square the current first: 100² = 10,000, then × 2 = 20,000 W. Using 100 × 2 = 200 forgets the square.

guided_steps.say: Power wasted in a cable: P = I²R. Square the current first.

guided_steps.hint: A hundred squared is ten thousand.
Should give the squared current back.

gold.display: A household uses 4,500 kWh of electricity in a year. Electricity costs 28p per kWh. Calculate the annual electricity bill in pounds.
gold.hint: Find the cost in pence, then divide by 100 for pounds.

misconceptions.message: That is the cost in pence. Divide by 100 for pounds: 126,000 ÷ 100 = £1,260.

guided_steps.say: Cost = energy × price in pence, then divide by 100 for pounds. 4,500 kWh at 28p each.

guided_steps.hint: Four and a half thousand times twenty-eight.

problem_bank.bronze_description: One equation, values already in the right units: pick it, substitute, state the unit.
problem_bank.silver_description: Convert the units first (watts to kilowatts, minutes to hours), or take two steps to the answer.
problem_bank.gold_description: Chain two equations, or rearrange, and mind every unit on the way.

worked_examples.question: A kettle is connected to the 230 V mains supply. A current of 9 A flows through it. Calculate the power of the kettle.
A 2.5 kW electric heater is used for 4 hours a day for 10 days. Electricity costs 25p per kWh. Calculate the total cost.
A resistor has a resistance of 50 Ω and a current of 0.6 A flowing through it. Calculate the power dissipated.

bronze.title: Bronze: one equation, right units
steps: Read the question and pick the matching equation: P = VI, P = I²R, or E = QV.
The values are already in base units (volts, amps, ohms, coulombs), so substitute straight in.
In P = I²R, square the current first. Always write the unit on your answer.

example.question: A lamp draws 3 A from a 12 V supply. Find its power.

silver.title: Silver: convert first, or take two steps
steps: Before any bill sum, change watts to kilowatts (÷1,000) and minutes to hours (÷60).
Cost = energy × price per kWh. Divide pence by 100 to reach pounds.

example.question: A 2,000 W heater runs for 30 minutes. Electricity is 20p per kWh. Find the cost in pence.

gold.title: Gold: chain the steps
steps: Gold questions need two moves: convert then energy then cost, or find power then energy.
For a transformer, Vp × Ip = Vs × Is; rearrange for the unknown. Check whether your board gives you this equation.
Keep every unit in line and check your answer by working back.

example.question: A cable of resistance 0.5 Ω carries 200 A. Find the power lost.

opener.label: Before any equations
opener.display:
A 2 kW heater, left on for 3 hours.
Electricity costs 30p per unit (a unit is one kWh).

steps.say: No formulas yet. Each hour, a 2 kW heater uses 2 units of electricity. Think in units.
steps.hint: Two units an hour, for three hours.

steps.say: That unit is a kilowatt-hour: energy (kWh) = power (kW) × time (hours). You just did 2 × 3. Now the money.
steps.pre: Each unit is 30p, so 6 units cost 6 × 30 =

steps.say: Cost = energy × price. That is the whole energy-bill method. The power itself comes from P = V × I, or P = I²R for a resistor.

bronze.display: A heater element of resistance 25 Ω carries a current of 4 A. Calculate the power in watts.
bronze.label: Together: your first one

steps.say: For a resistor, power is P = I²R. Square the current, then multiply by the resistance.
Now prove it hangs together by working back.

steps.done: Back to the 4 A we started with. 400 W is right.

silver.display: A 2,000 W oven runs for 45 minutes. Electricity costs 20p per kWh. Calculate the cost in pence.
silver.label: Together: convert first

steps.say: Two conversions before any sum: power to kilowatts, time to hours.

gold.display: A cable of resistance 0.5 Ω carries a current of 200 A. Find the power lost, then the energy wasted in 1 hour, in kWh.
gold.label: Together: chain two equations

steps.say: Two equations back to back: first P = I²R, then E = P × t.

steps.done: 20 kWh wasted every hour. That is why the grid uses high voltage and low current.
